messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC  post-call recap

Hi Alice / Raj  thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance qualification work for the ACME private/VPC deployment.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: Confirm we can hit ACME's production SLOs on a Private deployment (VPC peering / VPN) with Redwood running in your AWS account / VPC.
- Target SLOs discussed: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms, p99 tail <= 200 ms for single-request (non-streaming) paths. For streaming responses (chunked/keepalive) desired first-byte latency <= 120 ms and sustained per-token latency ~20-30 ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: initial load target 200 req/s sustained, burst to 800 concurrent token streams during peak with 50 concurrent long-poll/streaming sessions.
- Network constraints: your team called out an egress path through a NAT gateway + Transit Gateway peering between app VPC and inference VPC, plus an existing IPsec VPN used for on-prem dev. We flagged potential added RTT from cross-AZ routing and NAT.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) ACME to share the minimal network diagram (public/private subnets, Transit Gateway, NAT, firewall rules) and a sample VPN config  we noted Raj would share. (attachment: acme-network-diagram.png, acme-vpn-config.txt)
2) Redwood to provide a brief test plan + packet capture guidance so ACME can run an in-situ latency test from their application host to the Redwood inference endpoints. We attached our SLO proposal and a quick traceroute/pcap checklist. (attachment: redwood-vpc-slo-proposal.pdf, trace-20280729.pcap)
3) Technical handoff call: schedule a 60-min session with ACME infra + Connor (network lead) + our infra/solutions execs to walk the network path and validate MTU, TCP windowing, and TLS termination placement.
4) If in-VPC deployment: confirm whether ACME will accept AWS Transit Gateway peering or prefers site-to-site IPsec. We highlighted that Transit Gateway reduces egress NAT hops and typically gives lower and more predictable RTT.

Notes on internal latency budgets (for ACME app):
- App -> model fronting service (edge) must be under ~10 ms inside the VPC for us to hit the end-to-end p95 target. That means avoiding double NAT and keeping ENIs/SGs in the same AZ where possible.
- TLS termination: recommend mutual TLS between ACME app and Redwood sidecar in VPC to avoid extra proxy hops.

Please confirm when Raj can share the diagrams and whether Thursday or Friday morning next week works for the handoff call. I'll loop in Connor and Jordan on scheduling and we'll prepare the test plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa  this is great, appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 150 ms p95 target is what our product team wants for single-turn requests; for streaming we care most about first-byte latency (startup) since customers interact in quasi-realtime.
- Current infra: our inference VPC is behind a NAT gateway for egress; app VPC peered via Transit Gateway to inference VPC. We do route some traffic through a security proxy cluster which may add ~8-12 ms on average.
- We'll share the network diagram + the VPN config by EOD tomorrow (Raj is on it). Expect acme-network-diagram.png and a small packet capture.

Question: is Redwood able to run the test agent inside our inference VPC (an AMI / container we run) to hit the local inference endpoints to verify intra-VPC latency? That would help isolate the security proxy. If yes, what artifacts do you need to approve?

Also CC'ing our infra lead (infra@acme.com)  Raj, can you include the current VPN IPsec phase 1/2 config and any CloudWatch VPC flow logs for the handoff?

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Product, ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO / Private VPC  post-call recap

Jordan / Connor  forwarding ACME's confirmation. Key items for the handoff:

1) ACME is OK sharing: network diagram + VPN phase1/2 + VPC flow logs. They asked if we can run a test agent inside their inference VPC. Connor, we should be prepared with a hardened container/AMI and an RBAC checklist  they will want assurance on access and revocation.

2) From the call: watch out for the security proxy adding 8-12 ms. We should propose a quick internal-latency budget: app->proxy->inference-edge should be under 30 ms 95th; if proxy pushes >50 ms p95 we need to consider bypass (Transit Gateway route) or colocating a lightweight forwarder.

3) Test plan outline to attach to the handoff:
   - Synthetic test: 10k requests at target concurrency (200 rps sustained) from app-host -> inference endpoint to measure p50/p95/p99.
   - Streaming test: 50 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 minutes to measure first-byte and per-token latency.
   - Packet capture: 30-60s pcap during peak synthetic test; traceroute to capture RTT across AZs.

I'll draft the hardened agent image build instructions, minimal IAM policy, and a short checklist for ACME to run or allow us to run. Attaching SLO proposal PDFs now.

Marissa
